leftEvidence.title: The eye fills the body with light or darkness

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Jesus calls the eye the body’s lamp and contrasts a sound eye with an evil eye.
points.right: Jesus states that no one can serve two masters.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Whole-body light or darkness follows, ending with darkness mistaken for light.
points.right: Love and hate, devotion and contempt expose the division between God and Mammon.

payload.posture: The eye saying and two-master saying stand together between treasure and anxiety.

rightEvidence.title: God and Mammon cannot both be served

payload.tension: The discourse creates proximity without explicitly defining sound sight as service to God.
payload.title: Undivided sight and undivided service
